chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muthannā, from Zurārah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.
Concerning a man who kills his slave intentionally.
What expiation is upon him? He said: “The freeing of a slave, fasting two months, and charity upon sixty needy persons.”

key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةِ: the expiation required as legal atonement
key_terms.سِتِّينَ مِسْكِينًا: sixty needy persons who are to receive charity
key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ: charitable giving as part of the expiation
key_terms.صِيَامُ شَهْرَيْنِ: fasting for two months as a form of kaffarah
key_terms.عِتْقُ رَقَبَةٍ: freeing a slave as part of the prescribed expiation
key_terms.مُتَعَمِّدًا: intentionally; done deliberately and not by mistake

ai.seo_question: What kaffarah is required if a man intentionally kills his slave?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for one who intentionally kills his slave, specifying the required kaffarah. The expiation consists of freeing a slave, fasting for two months, and giving charity to sixty needy persons, highlighting the gravity of unlawful killing in Islamic law.
